subject: problems with setting up coverage layer in Distance

messages.author: 03985dae7a053c7a
messages.subject: problems with setting up coverage layer in Distance
parts:
I am trying to set up a transect system for my study area in Distance. When creating the coverage layer I get the error message: no grid could be generated and no grid points fell inside the survey area. Trying a smaller grid spacing also does not work.

Would anyone know how to fix this error?

Thanks,

Julia

messages.author: d6a29bde56bb826d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] problems with setting up coverage layer in Distance
parts:
Dear Julia,


You seen to have a shapefile issue (as well a minor units issue).


The easy part : I notice that the study region appears to be < 1 metre by 1 metre.


Looking at your map I see that the range is <1 in both the x (104.44 to 104.90) and y (-5.08 to -5.37) directions. I checked this by opening the map and reading the coordinates off the mouse location.

Next I checked your units.

File > Project Properties > Geographic

These were set to metres (you can change these here too as I am assuming they are incorrect.)


However, you do also seem to have a problem with your shapefile. I have tried a number of things to fix it. I imported it into R extracted the coordinates and re-made the shapefile using the shapefiles library. I did notice that there was a weird x and y limit on the coordinates. This could have been because the polygon was incomplete. I tried to fix this and the x and y limits made more sense. However, Distance is still not happy. I also tried importing your vertices by pasting directly into Distance so Distance created the shapefile. Again this did not fix the problem.


I therefore can only conclude that there is a problem with the vertices in your shapefile. Sometimes shapefiles become corrupted. Here are instructions to recover a corrupted shapefile http://support.esri.com/technical-article/000007161


Alternatively you could just try creating the shapefile again.


Best wishes,


Laura
